attempts.action: Test whether repeated high-amplitude sound bursts encode table output through pitch scaling.
attempts.command_or_step: Extract 60 s from video time 4 s; high-pass at 1.2 kHz; compute 5 ms RMS peaks; compare 105 ms clips by normalized correlation and resampling across playback rates 0.95-1.05.
attempts.notes: For audio-relative windows 7.5-15 s, 19-28 s, and 42-56 s, high-similarity repeated clips all matched best at rate 1.00. This does not expose a pitch bit in the sampled sound classes; it does not rule out other classes or channels.

attempts.action: Trace the first HUD-face sample and initial screen-wipe RNG consumption from the exact local source.
attempts.command_or_step: Inspect G_InitNew, G_DoLoadLevel, P_SpawnPlayer/ST_Start, G_Ticker, ST_Ticker, M_Random, D_Display, D_RunFrame, and wipe_initMelt; compare local m_random.c Git blob with patch base.
attempts.notes: M_ClearRandom precedes level setup; M_Random increments before reading; the first expected HUD sample is index 1 if P_Ticker starts no sound first. The transition wipe then consumes 320 M_Random calls and pauses game tics. The face-class mapping and any first-tic sound call remain unverified; no table observation or flag candidate.

attempts.action: Check whether the first visible post-wipe neutral face is the first random HUD selection.
attempts.command_or_step: Inspect all assignments to st_facecount and compare consecutive video face crops around the new-game transition.
attempts.notes: ST_initData resets st_faceindex but not the static st_facecount; ST_Start also leaves it untouched. The authorized gameplay video has a stable face through the early post-wipe segment, with a visible change only around 9.18 s. The first clear face therefore cannot be tied to table index 1 without reconstructing the carried timer and any face-priority events.
